investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent evals (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for ~148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing every required contract assertion.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. No preemption victims were available, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState evidence — causing all three remote-agent checks to fail. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration problem localized to the production-api Kubernetes cluster's peer-pod node pool; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure condition, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a user-facing outage.

If the affinity rules are overly narrow or stale, adding capacity elsewhere would not help without also updating the selector. The 4 non-matching nodes confirm this constraint is active.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck agent VMs from prior eval runs not being cleaned up: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (source-context line 1883) is responsible for teardown; if a prior run's cleanup failed, VM slots may remain occupied, contributing to exhaustion.

The API rejected the image generation request with HTTP error type "insufficient_quota" and code "credit_balance_exhausted" before any image could be produced. As a direct consequence, the SSE stream emitted a generation_error frame instead of generation_completed, imageUrlPresent remained false, and both required contract assertions failed. The failure is localized to the eval runner's OpenAI billing account and the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint; no sibling checks failed and no shared-dependency failure was flagged by the verifier.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent evals (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod remained unscheduled for ~148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing every required contract assertion.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. No preemption victims were available, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState evidence — causing all three remote-agent checks to fail. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration problem localized to the production-api Kubernetes cluster's peer-pod node pool; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure condition, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing agents or leaked/zombie pods, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's scheduling constraints restrict it to the 2 peer-pod nodes, but those nodes are full. If the affinity rules are overly narrow or stale, adding capacity elsewhere would not help without also updating the selector. The 4 non-matching nodes confirm this constraint is active.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck agent VMs from prior eval runs not being cleaned up: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (source-context line 1883) is responsible for teardown; if a prior run's cleanup failed, VM slots may remain occupied, contributing to exhaustion.
